blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.prompt: Let's call them together for a meeting.
exercises.why: **созвать → созовём** — perfective verb, 1st person plural: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.q: Давайте ___ (разделиться) на небольшие группы по четыре-пять человек.
exercises.prompt: Let's split into small groups of four or five people.
exercises.why: **разделиться → разделимся** — perfective verb, 1st person plural: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.prompt: The couch won't fit in the elevator.
exercises.why: **влезть → влезет** — perfective verb, 3rd person singular: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.q: Отправка этих писем не ___ (занять) много времени.
exercises.prompt: The sending of these letters won't take long.
exercises.why: **занять → займёт** — perfective verb, 3rd person singular: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.prompt: Can you break this twenty?
exercises.why: **разбить → разобьёте** — perfective verb, 2nd person plural: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.q: Господи! Ну борода у Вас! Выглядите ужасно! Вы всех детей ___ (распугать)!
exercises.prompt: God! What a beard you have! You look terrible! You're going to scare away the children.
exercises.why: **распугать → распугаете** — perfective verb, 2nd person plural: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.prompt: Let's saddle up our horses and go for a ride.
exercises.why: **оседлать → Оседлаем** — perfective verb, 1st person plural: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.prompt: I'll see you the day after tomorrow.
exercises.why: **увидеть → увижу** — perfective verb, 1st person singular: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.prompt: I will advise you on the matter.
exercises.why: **проконсультировать → проконсультирую** — perfective verb, 1st person singular: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.prompt: If you eat that much, you'll get fat.
exercises.why: **растолстеть → растолстеешь** — perfective verb, 2nd person singular: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.prompt: I have motion sickness.
exercises.why: **переносить → переношу** — present-type form, 1st person singular.

exercises.prompt: Which team will win?
exercises.why: **победить → победит** — perfective verb, 3rd person singular: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.prompt: I'll rephrase the question.
exercises.why: **перефразировать → перефразирую** — present-type form, 1st person singular.

exercises.q: Шеф нас за это по головке не ___ (погладить).
exercises.prompt: The boss won't pat us on the head for that.
exercises.why: **погладить → погладит** — perfective verb, 3rd person singular: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.prompt: Rescue parties are being organized.
exercises.why: **организоваться → Организуются** — perfective verb, 3rd person plural: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.prompt: Let's flip a coin.
exercises.why: **подбросить → подбросим** — perfective verb, 1st person plural: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.prompt: That will teach you a lesson.
exercises.why: **послужить → послужит** — perfective verb, 3rd person singular: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.prompt: Let's slip away quietly.
exercises.why: **улизнуть → улизнём** — perfective verb, 1st person plural: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.prompt: If you lie, your tongue will be split in two!
exercises.why: **раздвоиться → раздвоится** — perfective verb, 3rd person singular: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.

exercises.prompt: When will Yuko come to Denver?
exercises.why: **приехать → приедет** — perfective verb, 3rd person singular: it has no present tense; the present-type ending gives the future.
